 "cells": [

   "id": "f1aaf511",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# Time Series - Clusters"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "687d6deb",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "A `TimeSeriesCluster` holds series of the **same variable from different sites**, like a network of weather stations or rain gauges. Unlike a `TimeSeriesCollection`, which accepts miscellaneous data, a cluster can compare its series against each other: how correlated the sites are, and how one site can fill the gaps of another.\n",
    "\n",
    "This tutorial builds a synthetic network of five temperature stations in two sub-regions:\n",
    "\n",
    "| Station | Sub-region | Range | Gaps |\n",
    "|---|---|---|---|\n",
    "| `S1` | west | full year | 1 large (30d) |\n",
    "| `S2` | west | full year | none |\n",
    "| `S3` | west | full year | none |\n",
    "| `S4` | east | Mar-Dec (shorter) | none |\n",
    "| `S5` | east | full year | 1 small (3d) |\n",
    "\n",
    "Covered here:\n",
    "\n",
    "- Loading the stations into a `TemperatureSeriesCluster`\n",
    "- Viewing data availability and all series together\n",
    "- Correlation between stations via `get_correlation()`\n",
    "- Gap filling from other stations via `regionalize()`, comparing uniform and inverse-distance weights\n",
    "\n",
    "```{seealso}\n",
    "Check out the {doc}`Time Series - Collections <timeseries_07_collection>` tutorial first.\n",
    "```"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "26d30523",
   "metadata": {},

    "import sys\n",
    "import copy\n",
    "from pathlib import Path\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "\n",
    "# Install `plans` in `google.colab`.\n",
    "# Use `pip install plans` for other environments.\n",
    "\n",
    "if \"google.colab\" in sys.modules:\n",
    "    import os\n",
    "    os.system(f\"{sys.executable} -m pip install -q plans\")\n",
    "\n",
    "from plans.datasets import TemperatureSeriesCluster\n",
    "from plans.datasets.analyst import Bivar\n",
    "\n",
    "# This avoids warnings related to uninstalled fonts\n",
    "import logging\n",
    "logging.getLogger('matplotlib.font_manager').setLevel(logging.ERROR)\n",
    "\n",
    "OUTPUT_DIR = Path(\"outputs/time-series-cluster\")\n",
    "OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n",
    "print(f\"Outputs will be saved to: ./{OUTPUT_DIR}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=7)  # ensure reproducibility"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "c355c607",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Build a synthetic station network\n",
    "\n",
    "Each station gets the same cycle, a weather anomaly common to the whole region, a weather anomaly of its own sub-region, and some local shocks. The anomalies have memory (an autoregressive process), so warm or cold spells last for some days. Stations in the same sub-region share more signal, so they should correlate more."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "353ea125",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:53:30.241403Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T21:53:30.240869Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T21:53:30.258907Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T21:53:30.257583Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "n = 365\n",
    "t = np.arange(n)\n",
    "\n",
    "def make_anomaly(phi, sd):\n",
    "    # autoregressive anomaly: a[t] = phi * a[t-1] + shock\n",
    "    a = np.zeros(n)\n",
    "    e = rng.normal(loc=0, scale=sd, size=n)\n",
    "    for i in range(1, n):\n",
    "        a[i] = phi * a[i - 1] + e[i]\n",
    "    return a\n",
    "\n",
    "cycle = 18 + 4 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * (t - 100) / 365)\n",
    "anomaly_region = make_anomaly(phi=0.8, sd=1.0)\n",
    "anomaly_subregion = {\n",
    "    \"west\": make_anomaly(phi=0.8, sd=1.2),\n",
    "    \"east\": make_anomaly(phi=0.8, sd=1.2),\n",
    "}\n",
    "\n",
    "# stations: sub-region and coordinates (km)\n",
    "stations = pd.DataFrame({\n",
    "    \"Name\": [\"S1\", \"S2\", \"S3\", \"S4\", \"S5\"],\n",
    "    \"Subregion\": [\"west\", \"west\", \"west\", \"east\", \"east\"],\n",
    "    \"X\": [0, 2, 1, 10, 11],\n",
    "    \"Y\": [0, 1, 3, 2, 0],\n",
    "})\n",
    "\n",
    "dates = pd.date_range(start=\"2021-01-01\", periods=n, freq=\"D\")\n",
    "dc_series = {}\n",
    "for _, row in stations.iterrows():\n",
    "    dc_series[row[\"Name\"]] = (\n",
    "        cycle\n",
    "        + anomaly_region\n",
    "        + anomaly_subregion[row[\"Subregion\"]]\n",
    "        + rng.normal(loc=0, scale=0.8, size=n)\n",
    "    )"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "0b4adc3f",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Lets look at where the stations are:"
   ]

  {

   "source": [
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4, 3))\n",
    "colors = {\"west\": \"tab:blue\", \"east\": \"tab:orange\"}\n",
    "for _, row in stations.iterrows():\n",
    "    ax.scatter(row[\"X\"], row[\"Y\"], color=colors[row[\"Subregion\"]], s=40)\n",
    "    ax.annotate(row[\"Name\"], (row[\"X\"], row[\"Y\"]), xytext=(5, 5), textcoords=\"offset points\")\n",
    "ax.set_xlim(-2, 13)\n",
    "ax.set_ylim(-2, 5)\n",
    "ax.set_aspect(\"equal\")\n",
    "ax.set_xlabel(\"X (km)\")\n",
    "ax.set_ylabel(\"Y (km)\")\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "877d244e",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Now add the gaps. Before removing the values of the large gap in `S1`, keep them as the **truth**, so we can later check how well the gap was filled:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,
   "id": "bd211396",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:53:30.405277Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T21:53:30.404971Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T21:53:30.425499Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T21:53:30.424702Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "stream",
     "name": "stdout",
     "text": "['outputs\\\\time-series-cluster\\\\S1.csv', 'outputs\\\\time-series-cluster\\\\S2.csv', 'outputs\\\\time-series-cluster\\\\S3.csv', 'outputs\\\\time-series-cluster\\\\S4.csv', 'outputs\\\\time-series-cluster\\\\S5.csv']\n"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# large gap in S1 -- keep the truth\n",
    "GAP = slice(150, 180)\n",
    "truth = dc_series[\"S1\"][GAP].copy()\n",
    "dc_series[\"S1\"][GAP] = np.nan\n",
    "\n",
    "# small gap in S5\n",
    "dc_series[\"S5\"][200:203] = np.nan\n",
    "\n",
    "# save files -- S4 starts later\n",
    "ls_files = []\n",
    "for name, values in dc_series.items():\n",
    "    df = pd.DataFrame({\"datetime\": dates, \"T\": values})\n",
    "    if name == \"S4\":\n",
    "        df = df.iloc[60:]\n",
    "    file = OUTPUT_DIR / f\"{name}.csv\"\n",
    "    df.to_csv(file, sep=\";\", index=False)\n",
    "    ls_files.append(str(file))\n",
    "print(ls_files)"
   ]
  },
  {

   "source": [
    "## Load into a Time Series Cluster\n",
    "\n",
    "Like a collection, a cluster is loaded from an info table. The `X` and `Y` columns are the station coordinates, used later for inverse-distance weights. Here we use `TemperatureSeriesCluster`, a cluster ready for temperature series:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "e8dfaa13",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:53:30.430253Z",

    }

   "source": [
    "info = pd.DataFrame({\n",
    "    \"Name\": stations[\"Name\"],\n",
    "    \"Alias\": stations[\"Name\"],\n",
    "    \"File\": ls_files,\n",
    "    \"VarField\": \"T\",\n",
    "    \"DtField\": \"datetime\",\n",
    "    \"Units\": \"C\",\n",
    "    \"X\": stations[\"X\"],\n",
    "    \"Y\": stations[\"Y\"],\n",
    "    \"Code\": stations[\"Name\"],\n",
    "    \"Source\": \"synthetic\",\n",
    "    \"Description\": \"daily air temperature, \" + stations[\"Subregion\"] + \" sub-region\",\n",
    "    \"Color\": \"tab:red\",\n",
    "})\n",
    "info_file = OUTPUT_DIR / \"info.csv\"\n",
    "info.to_csv(info_file, sep=\";\", index=False)\n",
    "\n",
    "tsc = TemperatureSeriesCluster(name=\"Network\")\n",
    "tsc.load_data(table_file=info_file)\n",
    "tsc.catalog[[\"name\", \"x\", \"y\", \"start\", \"end\", \"variable_min\", \"variable_max\"]]"
   ]

    "## Correlation between stations\n",
    "\n",
    "The `.get_correlation()` method computes the correlation matrix between all stations, using only the time steps where both have data. Pairs with fewer overlapping steps than `min_overlap` are set to `NaN`:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 9,
   "id": "57f21eaa",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:53:32.781593Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T21:53:32.781101Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T21:53:32.878123Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T21:53:32.876505Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "execute_result",
     "metadata": {},
     "data": {

     },

    }

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "f0cee9a0",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The two sub-regions show up as two blocks: stations of the same sub-region correlate around 0.95, while stations of different sub-regions stay around 0.7. Spearman correlation is also available with `method=\"spearman\"`.\n",
    "\n",
    "```{note}\n",
    "With a strong cycle, correlation is partly driven by the shared cycle itself. Even unrelated sites under the same climate correlate well.\n",
    "```"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "569d4b35",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Filling gaps from other stations\n",
    "\n",
    "The `.regionalize()` method fills the gaps of every station with a weighted average of the other stations, on the time steps where they have data. Observed values are never changed. Two weighting methods are available:\n",
    "\n",
    "- `average`: all other stations get the same weight.\n",
    "- `idw`: inverse distance weighting, closer stations get more weight.\n",
    "\n",
    "Check the share of each station in the weights for `S1`:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 11,
   "id": "f140ec50",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:53:33.232029Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T21:53:33.231409Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T21:53:33.252439Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T21:53:33.250915Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "execute_result",
     "metadata": {},
     "data": {
      "text/plain": "    average   idw\nS2     0.25  0.47\nS3     0.25  0.33\nS4     0.25  0.10\nS5     0.25  0.10",
      "text/html": "<div>\n<style scoped>\n    .dataframe tbody tr th:only-of-type {\n        vertical-align: middle;\n    }\n\n    .dataframe tbody tr th {\n        vertical-align: top;\n    }\n\n    .dataframe thead th {\n        text-align: right;\n    }\n</style>\n<table border=\"1\" class=\"dataframe\">\n  <thead>\n    <tr style=\"text-align: right;\">\n      <th></th>\n      <th>average</th>\n      <th>idw</th>\n    </tr>\n  </thead>\n  <tbody>\n    <tr>\n      <th>S2</th>\n      <td>0.25</td>\n      <td>0.47</td>\n    </tr>\n    <tr>\n      <th>S3</th>\n      <td>0.25</td>\n      <td>0.33</td>\n    </tr>\n    <tr>\n      <th>S4</th>\n      <td>0.25</td>\n      <td>0.10</td>\n    </tr>\n    <tr>\n      <th>S5</th>\n      <td>0.25</td>\n      <td>0.10</td>\n    </tr>\n  </tbody>\n</table>\n</div>"
     },
     "execution_count": 11
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "df_weights = pd.DataFrame(\n",
    "    {method: tsc.get_weights_by_name(name=\"S1\", method=method) for method in [\"average\", \"idw\"]},\n",
    "    index=[\"S2\", \"S3\", \"S4\", \"S5\"],\n",
    ")\n",
    "df_weights = df_weights / df_weights.sum()\n",
    "df_weights.round(2)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "ff97f17b",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Since `.regionalize()` changes the data in place, lets run each method on a copy of the cluster:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 12,
   "id": "3fad08fa",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:53:33.256796Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T21:53:33.256307Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T21:53:36.249153Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T21:53:36.247662Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "dc_clusters = {}\n",
    "for method in [\"average\", \"idw\"]:\n",
    "    dc_clusters[method] = copy.deepcopy(tsc)\n",
    "    dc_clusters[method].regionalize(method=method)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "d3f208e4",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The gap in `S1` is now closed:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 13,
   "id": "4447cb43",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:53:36.252997Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T21:53:36.252326Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T21:53:37.270406Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T21:53:37.268851Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "display_data",
     "metadata": {},

      "text/plain": "<Figure size 1003.94x472.441 with 3 Axes>",
      "image/png": ""
     }
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "tsc_idw = dc_clusters[\"idw\"]\n",
    "tsc_idw.view_specs[\"layout\"] = \"full\"\n",
    "tsc_idw.view()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "5873abc3",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "### How good is the filling?\n",
    "\n",
    "Since we kept the truth, we can compare the filled values against it using the `Bivar` metrics:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 14,
   "id": "39573a9a",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:53:37.274957Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T21:53:37.274390Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T21:53:37.810939Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T21:53:37.809308Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "execute_result",
     "metadata": {},
     "data": {
      "text/plain": "             RMSE       MAE      Bias        R2\naverage  1.952558  1.547067  7.487313  0.022263\nidw      1.040685  0.824099  2.649993  0.722251",
      "text/html": "<div>\n<style scoped>\n    .dataframe tbody tr th:only-of-type {\n        vertical-align: middle;\n    }\n\n    .dataframe tbody tr th {\n        vertical-align: top;\n    }\n\n    .dataframe thead th {\n        text-align: right;\n    }\n</style>\n<table border=\"1\" class=\"dataframe\">\n  <thead>\n    <tr style=\"text-align: right;\">\n      <th></th>\n      <th>RMSE</th>\n      <th>MAE</th>\n      <th>Bias</th>\n      <th>R2</th>\n    </tr>\n  </thead>\n  <tbody>\n    <tr>\n      <th>average</th>\n      <td>1.952558</td>\n      <td>1.547067</td>\n      <td>7.487313</td>\n      <td>0.022263</td>\n    </tr>\n    <tr>\n      <th>idw</th>\n      <td>1.040685</td>\n      <td>0.824099</td>\n      <td>2.649993</td>\n      <td>0.722251</td>\n    </tr>\n  </tbody>\n</table>\n</div>"
     },
     "execution_count": 14
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "gap_dates = dates[GAP]\n",
    "dc_filled = {}\n",
    "for method, cluster in dc_clusters.items():\n",
    "    ts = cluster.collection[\"S1\"]\n",
    "    s = ts.data.set_index(ts.dtfield)[ts.varfield]\n",
    "    dc_filled[method] = s.loc[gap_dates].values\n",
    "\n",
    "df_metrics = pd.DataFrame(\n",
    "    {method: Bivar.get_metrics(observed=truth, predicted=filled) for method, filled in dc_filled.items()}\n",
    ").T\n",
    "df_metrics[[\"RMSE\", \"MAE\", \"Bias\", \"R2\"]]"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "bbb765ed",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "And see it on the gap window:"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 15,
   "id": "30ca7c89",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-10-30T21:53:37.815657Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-10-30T21:53:37.815118Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-10-30T21:53:38.063745Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-10-30T21:53:38.062255Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "output_type": "display_data",
     "metadata": {},
     "data": {
      "text/plain": "<Figure size 1050x450 with 1 Axes>",
      "image/png": ""
     }
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3))\n",
    "ax.plot(gap_dates, truth, color=\"black\", label=\"truth\")\n",
    "ax.plot(gap_dates, dc_filled[\"average\"], color=\"tab:gray\", linestyle=\"--\", label=\"average\")\n",
    "ax.plot(gap_dates, dc_filled[\"idw\"], color=\"tab:blue\", label=\"idw\")\n",
    "ax.set_ylabel(\"Temperature (C)\")\n",
    "ax.legend(frameon=False)\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "c22ff71b",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Inverse distance weighting follows the truth much closer, since it relies mostly on `S2` and `S3`, which share the west sub-region weather. The uniform average gives half of the weight to the east stations, which have their own weather.\n",
    "\n",
    "```{warning}\n",
    "`.regionalize()` takes the other stations values as they are. Stations with systematically different levels (e.g., temperature at different elevations) will bias the filling.\n",
    "```"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "c02c1c88",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Recap\n",
    "\n",
    "- A `TimeSeriesCluster` holds same-variable series from different sites, loaded from an info table with station coordinates.\n",
    "- The `series` and `correlation` layouts show the series together and the correlation between sites; the default layout shows data availability.\n",
    "- `get_correlation()` compares sites on their overlapping time steps.\n",
    "- `regionalize()` fills gaps from other sites, with uniform or inverse-distance weights."
   ]
  }
